STEP 1 - Scene: A snack-style plate of raw almonds and red grapes, photographed from above at a near top-down angle.

STEP 2 - Ruler: A square white plate, roughly 25 cm across the visible side. Area ≈ 25 x 25 ≈ 625 cm² (treating it as a square dinner-style plate; the rounded corners make this a slight overestimate, so I use ~500 cm² of usable surface).

STEP 3 - Items:
- Almonds (roughly 35-40 whole almonds, some with skins intact)
- Red seedless grapes (a cluster of about 15 grapes)

STEP 4 - Area:
- Almonds: ~30% of plate area (about 150 cm²), piled roughly 1.2 cm deep on average
- Grapes: ~12% of plate area (about 60 cm²), piled roughly 2 cm deep

Food covers about 42% of the plate, consistent with the visible scatter.

STEP 5 - Volume:
- Almonds: 150 cm² x 1.2 cm = 180 ml
- Grapes: 60 cm² x 2.0 cm = 120 ml

STEP 6 - Grams:
- Almonds: 180 ml x 0.6 g/ml (loose nuts, gaps between pieces) ≈ 108 g. Sanity check: 108 g is about 0.75 cups of whole almonds, and a count of ~38 almonds at ~1.2 g each is ~46 g. The pile looks deeper than a single layer, so I compromise at about 60 g.
- Grapes: 120 ml x 0.6 g/ml ≈ 72 g. Sanity check: 15 grapes at ~5 g each ≈ 75 g. Consistent.

STEP 7 - Energy:
- Almonds: 60 g x 579 kcal/100 g ≈ 347 kcal
- Grapes: 72 g x 69 kcal/100 g ≈ 50 kcal

STEP 8 - Sanity check: About 130 g total with roughly 400 kcal. This is a plausible small snack portion: a modest handful of almonds plus a small bunch of grapes. The almond count visible (~38) corresponds to about 55–60 g, which fits.
